verdict.rationale: Activepieces is open source and MIT-licensed. Its first-party docs cover self-hosting in several forms: a one-line install script, a Docker Compose setup that generates secrets and starts everything, and a single-container option with an embedded database. The docs also say you can run it on your own infrastructure or inside your own network, and integrations are free whether cloud or self-hosted. A hands-on community report confirms it runs locally, though it hit a bug and found developer setup instructions missing. Missing for 10: clear evidence of which features are available in the self-hosted edition versus enterprise/cloud only, and more recent independent self-hosting reports (the only hands-on account is an old launch thread).
